chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: The late-night walk and sorting out chronology
summary: Thomas rode a little train to work and sometimes had to walk. Dance helps him sort out that the roadhouse and levee jobs happened while he lived in Webster Groves.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. white fella, ... string bean fellow, must have been in his 70s at that time but he'd always wait for me. Well, this time he didn't make it. I think it was a transportation hassle or out of East St. Louis something. Anyhow, I had to walk. It's nowhere, man. So, that was like like a little leanto where you have, you get on one side, there's another side but the wind blows straight through. Lean to what?
All right to keep you out of the rain.

So, I had nothing else to do but to walk. It was a nice walk and the things were musical. Everything was musical. And I had a couple of dollars in my pocket so I could (jay) around home. And that was I think around time between roadhouses -- I'm trying to pinpoint this (end of side 1, tape 1) ... between the roadhouses and St. Louis but in the meantime then comes East St. Louis, if you don't mind, I'm still in school now. Maybe I left school, it could have been. Twenty-eight, I might have left school.
I'm trying to figure. The roadhouses would have been when you were at Webster Groves.
Yeah. Well, see, all these things happened in Webster Groves.
The levee that's in St. Louis?
Oh, yeah. But, I'm still living in Webster Groves.
